workstream.name: ecl v1 — the real interpreter (design/workstream-v1.md)
workstream.unlocks: Milestone 11 (stdlib-str-csv-json-table-http) authors the embedded stdlib modules once against merged binding semantics; Milestone 12 (v1-acceptance) tags 0.1.0 with one binding kind.

problemStatement: ecl bindings carry a hidden word|value kind tag: `def` publishes a word whose reference applies its body, `set` publishes a value whose reference pushes it. The tag places a burden on the reader — bare `foo`'s behavior depends on how it was bound, and for quotations the same-looking value behaves oppositely. The 2026-08-17 ruling (workstream Decisions Made; Milestone 10) replaces the tag with uniform application plus visible literal capture, before the stdlib milestone so embedded modules are authored once against final semantics.
solutionSummary: Make `v 'name set` observationally `v literal (-- value) 'name def`: set/setp become prelude source words that publish a word binding whose stored body is the literal capture `((v) first)` with a synthesized `(-- value)` effect annotation, uniformly at top level and in modules. Bare reference then always applies a body; the `Binding.value` union arm and the value arms of both publication types are deleted; `body` becomes total over def/set-published names and `which`/`see` print the stored body honestly. One idiom-recognition family fast-paths the capture shape observationally invisibly. The prelude placement is licensed by a grounded machine invariant: `scheduleWord` keeps the caller's scope for core words (src/machine.zig:4270), so `def` executing inside `set`'s body writes the unit's current scope — session at top level, module root inside a module body.
currentStateAnalysis: At HEAD (master, M1–M9 executed): src/env.zig:50 defines `Binding = union(enum){ word, value, builtin, native }`; TopPublication (:149) and ModulePublication (:157) carry value arms (module values have no effect — the callable-requires-ValidatedEffect/value-cannot-carry split); BindingSpec.fromTop/fromModule (:176–219) construct the value arms. src/machine.zig:3750 `executeResolved` dispatches `.value => pushBorrowed`, `.word => scheduleWord` with cross-home effect frames, and prepares immediate effect checks only for builtin/native; :4270 `scheduleWord` keeps the caller's scope when resolved_home is null (core words) — the write-target fact that licenses prelude set. src/definition_prims.zig registers set/setp as builtins (:30–32) sharing `define()`/DefineDriver with def/defp (Mode enum :16); annotation recognition is skipped for set/setp by the word_binding test (:56, :66); the driver pops the body mid-drive when the first popped item is an annotation (:159–160); `body` type-errors on non-word bindings (:319–324); `which` prints kind strings 'def/set/primitive/native' (:369–374); `see` renders value bindings as `<value> 'name set/setp` (:483–517); `def expected a list body; use set for values` (:249). src/primitive_docs.zig:39,41 carry set/setp metadata (90 entries). src/prelude.ecl has 60 `### def` blocks; src/prelude.zig evaluates it into the building core with a root scope, so prelude `'set def` replaces the builtin cell. src/idioms.zig PatternAtom `.constant` matches a single non-word form only — the two-form capture `((v) first)` is unrecognized today, so partial-built quotations take the generic path. test/reference_snapshots.zig holds an inline ohsnap transcript with no set/which/see cases; test/acceptance's two setp fixtures (body-extraction.ecl, modules-privacy.ecl) produce identical output under the merge. The source audit logs (does not assert) the prelude block count. Only src/tests/definition_test.zig and src/tests/module_test.zig pin kind-specific observables; concurrency/oom/fuzz set usages have equivalence-preserved outcomes.

operationalConsiderations.externalSystemAccess: Not applicable — ecl is a single-binary interpreter and this gameplan adds no external system. The one external surface, the native-extension wire ABI, is untouched: ModulePublication.native, NativeCallable, and the descriptor format are not modified by any patch.
operationalConsiderations.crossRuntimeContracts: The `.eclmod` ABI-v1 contract (src/native/abi.zig, validated by src/native_descriptor.zig) is unchanged — native words already publish as effect-carrying callables and keep doing so. The human contract surfaces are design/SPEC.md and design/INTERPRETER.md, rewritten in patch 5 in the same gameplan so docs and binary land together. src/prelude.ecl is embedded at build time (@embedFile in src/prelude.zig), so there is no runtime producer/consumer skew: a binary always carries the prelude matching its code.
operationalConsiderations.failureBehavior: Two deliberate failure-behavior changes, both owned by patch 3: (1) error-site attribution shifts into the sugar — an underflowing `set` now raises from `swap` (and a non-symbol name raises from `def`) with `set` as the trace parent, pinned by updated tests; (2) a defect in the new prelude blocks fails bootstrap with error.InvalidPrelude at Session init, which fails every test in every gate immediately — the failure mode is loud and pre-merge, not latent. The `zig build test-oom` exhaustive allocation-failure sweep automatically covers the sugar's new allocation points (literal capture list construction, effect materialization) because it injects by ordinal across the whole initialized-Session lifetime.
operationalConsiderations.concurrencyAndIdempotency: No new concurrent path. Binding publication continues through the existing single-writer funnel (publishTopCursor/publishModuleCursor, snapshot leases with sequentially consistent handoff) — patch 3 changes what is published, not how. Idiom recognition (patch 2) is a per-application structural guard with no cache and no invalidation, per the existing recognizer discipline. The scheduler suites at 1 and N workers plus the TSan gate run unchanged and must stay green at every patch.
operationalConsiderations.rollbackStrategy: No persistent state anywhere in the change: no migrations, no on-disk formats, no external writes. Reverting the patch stack restores the builtin set/setp, the Binding.value arm, the snapshot transcript, and the docs in one git operation; sequencing (stubs → invisible recognition → flip → dead-arm removal → docs) means any prefix of the stack is a green, shippable tree.

mergabilityStrategy.featureFlagStrategy: Ungated. ecl has no feature-flag infrastructure (the only env toggles are ECL_WORKERS/ECL_PATH/ECL_NATIVE_DIAGNOSTICS, none of which gates semantics), and the workstream ruling (Decisions Made, 2026-08-17) ships this as a pre-0.1.0 semantics replacement — prerelease is when to break. Gating the binding representation would double every reflection, snapshot, and differential expectation for a toggle no one would keep. Safety comes from sequencing instead: every intermediate tree is green, and the single BEHAVIOR patch is the smallest possible flip.
mergabilityStrategy.patchOrderingStrategy: Early INFRA: patch 1 lands skipped test stubs naming their implementing patches; patch 2 lands the capture-shape idiom recognition, which is observationally invisible today (the shape is already producible via literal/partial) and differentially proven. Middle BEHAVIOR: patch 3 is the one semantic flip — prelude set/setp replace the builtins, tests and snapshots update together. Late INFRA: patch 4 deletes the now-unproducible value arms (compile-atomic exhaustive-switch sweep), and patch 5 rewrites SPEC.md/INTERPRETER.md to the merged semantics.

requiredChanges.description: Append `### def set` and `### def setp` blocks. set body: `(swap literal swap (-- value) swap def)` with annotation `(value name -- : "Bind a value as a constant word in the current scope.")`; setp body: `(swap literal swap (-- value) swap defp)` with annotation `(value name -- : "Bind a private module value as a constant word.")`. The nested `(-- value)` is inert during the prelude's own definition (nested markers are inert) and becomes the synthesized effect annotation for every set-published binding.

functionalChanges.description: `v 'name set` at top level publishes a word binding whose stored body is the literal capture `((v) first)` with declared effect `(-- value)`; bare reference applies the body and pushes exactly v — observationally `v literal (-- value) 'name def`.
`setp` and module-body `set` publish module constants as word bindings carrying the synthesized `(-- value)` effect, satisfying the mandatory module-effect rule; privacy is unchanged.
`'name body` on a set-bound name returns the capture body `((v) first)` instead of raising `'type` — body is total over def/set-published bindings (builtin/native still error).
`which` reports set-bound names with the `def` kind string and shows their `(-- value)` effect; the `set` kind label no longer appears in which output.
`see` on a set-bound name prints the stored capture body plus the `(-- value)` annotation ending `'name def` (or `defp` for privates) — no reconstruction of set-sugar spelling.
Top-level `setp` fails through defp's module-root check: the raised `'domain` error names defp as the raiser with setp in the trace.
set's failure sites shift into its body: stack underflow raises from `swap` and a non-symbol name raises from `def`, each with `set` as the trace parent (message kinds unchanged: 'underflow/'type).

`'set see` and `'setp see` print prelude source definitions instead of `<primitive>`; set/setp leave the builtin vocabulary (88 primitives, 62 prelude blocks) while keeping their names and stack protocols.

Cross-home references to module constants pass through the standard word effect-check frame with the `(-- value)` contract; a conforming constant application is indistinguishable from today's value push in result terms.

contextResources.why: The builtin set/setp being retired live here, sharing define()/DefineDriver with def/defp (Mode :16, install :27–39, annotation scan and mid-drive body pop :112–260, publish funnel :255–263). body/doc/which/see drivers (:287–560) define the exact reflection strings the stubs and snapshot cases pin: which kind strings :369–374, see rendering arms :483–517, def's list-body error text :249.

Binding (:50), TopPublication (:149), ModulePublication (:157), BindingSpec.fromTop/fromModule (:176–219), and ValidatedEffect.parse (:94–147) — the arms patch 4 deletes and the effect representation the synthesized `(-- value)` annotation must satisfy (exactly one `--` separator among words; inputs 0, outputs 1).

executeResolved (:3750–3797) is the dispatch whose .value arm dies; scheduleWord (:4263–4288) proves the write-target rule licensing prelude set — a core word's body keeps the caller's scope and home, so def inside set writes the unit's current scope and module-root checks stay dynamic; cross-home word applications already install effect-check frames, which is how the `(-- value)` contract is enforced. continueWithIdiom at :3762–3769 is the direct-context recognition entry patch 2 extends.

PatternAtom/RegistryEntry (:50–62), the comptime registry (:157+), and the matcher (:391–430) define the recognition discipline the new capture entries must follow: pattern words resolved in the application environment guard selection, mismatch falls through to the generic path, and every entry ships with differential coverage in the existing harness.

The `### def` block convention, annotation-with-docstring house style, and the literal/partial definitions the sugar composes; prelude.zig shows bootstrap evaluates prelude.ecl against the building core (a prelude 'set def replaces the builtin cell, and the stack must end empty); primitive_docs.zig is the closed metadata table whose set/setp rows leave with the builtins.

Workstream Milestone 10 and the Decisions Made entry (2026-08-17) are the ruling this gameplan implements: equivalence law, uniform `(-- value)` synthesis, honest see/which, prelude placement gated on the write-target rule. SPEC.md's current Bindings/Definition annotations/Modules sections are the pre-state contract — everything there except the kind tag must survive verbatim.

The snapshot gate is one inline ohsnap transcript over -e cases — new cases mean editing the cases array and the transcript together, and snapshot changes are intentional review events. The source audit lexes prelude.ecl and requires every top-level definition to be a `### def <name>` block with a matching quoted name; AGENTS.md's Embedded prelude section requires a meaningful nonempty docstring per block.

The as-built sections patch 5 rewrites: Values and memory / Environments (Binding snapshot contents), Typed publication and control state (the callable/value ValidatedEffect split), and Idiom recognition (the bridged-word list gaining the capture entries). Descriptions must match the post-patch-4 code exactly.

acceptanceCriteria: `3 'x set x` leaves 3; `(dup *) 'q set q` leaves the quotation `(dup *)`; both via word bindings whose stored body is `((v) first)` — verified by tests and snapshot cases.

`'x body` on a set-bound name returns the capture body; `'x which` prints the `def` kind string with the `(-- value)` effect; `'x see` prints the stored body plus `(-- value)` ending `'x def` and round-trips through the reader.

Module `set`/`setp` publish constants carrying the synthesized `(-- value)` ValidatedEffect (inputs 0, outputs 1); cross-home references pass the effect-check frame; top-level `setp` raises `'domain` through defp's module-root check.

set/setp are `### def` blocks in src/prelude.ecl with docstrings (audit reports 62 documented blocks); they are absent from definition_prims install() and primitive_docs.zig (88 primitive entries); `'set see` shows the source definition.
After patch 4, `Binding` has no value arm, TopPublication is word-only, ModulePublication is word|native, and every switch over these types compiles exhaustively.

The capture-shape idiom entries pass the differential harness — value equality, representation parity, error kind/payload equality, bit-identical floats — and the 1/N-worker suites assert identical outcomes.

`zig build test` (including snapshots and the source audit), `zig build test-workers`, and `zig build test-oom` are green at every patch boundary; the two setp acceptance fixtures (body-extraction, modules-privacy) pass unchanged.

design/SPEC.md and design/INTERPRETER.md describe exactly the merged semantics: no kind-tag language, set/setp documented as normative ecl equivalences, INTERPRETER's publication typestates match the shrunk unions.

explicitOpinions.opinion: set/setp are prelude source, not host primitives with equivalent behavior.
explicitOpinions.rationale: The milestone gated source placement on the write-target rule; grounding resolved it at HEAD: scheduleWord (src/machine.zig:4270) keeps the caller's scope and home for core words, so def inside set's body writes the unit's current scope — session at top level, module root in a module body — and defp's module-root check stays dynamic. A dedicated test pins this rule (stub in patch 1) so a future scoping change cannot silently break the sugar. Source placement also follows the standard-library placement rule: the definitions are compact and their performance does not justify host idioms.

explicitOpinions.opinion: The `(-- value)` effect is synthesized uniformly, at top level and in modules.
explicitOpinions.rationale: One definition with no context-sensitivity: top-level def accepts optional annotations, module def requires the effect portion, so unconditional attachment satisfies both. The contract (0 inputs, 1 output) is true of every literal capture by construction. Ruled in the milestone DoD (agreed 2026-08-17).

explicitOpinions.opinion: see/which print stored bodies with no reconstruction of set-sugar spelling.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Ruled 2026-08-17: reconstruction would be the deleted kind tag reappearing as a display heuristic. Consequence accepted: `'x see` prints `((3) first) (-- value) 'x def`, which is honest, re-readable source; a captured task handle makes see non-re-readable exactly as today's value display did.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Error-site attribution shifts into the sugar (FC-7) are accepted, not compensated.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Follows necessarily from prelude placement, which was ruled. Compensating (e.g. a special pre-check) would reintroduce host logic the placement removed. Error kinds are unchanged ('underflow/'type); traces name set as the parent, matching how every other prelude word reports.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Idiom recognition covers the capture shape in both direct and combinator contexts, and lands before the flip as an independent INFRA patch.
explicitOpinions.rationale: The shape ((v) first) is already producible today via literal/partial, so recognition is observationally invisible now and differentially provable before any semantics change — sequencing it first keeps the BEHAVIOR patch minimal. Direct-context entries serve prelude/core constants; combinator-context [capture, op] and [capture, swap, op] entries make partial-built quotations reach kernels, honoring the milestone's 'constants and partial results' commitment.

explicitOpinions.opinion: The dead Binding.value arm is deleted in a separate INFRA patch after the flip, not bundled into it.
explicitOpinions.rationale: After patch 3 no language path can construct a value binding, so arm deletion is observationally invisible — but it is compile-atomic across env.zig/machine.zig/definition_prims.zig (Zig's exhaustive switches force simultaneous edits). Separating it keeps the BEHAVIOR patch reviewable and makes the union shrink a mechanical, obviously-safe diff.

No flag infrastructure exists; the workstream ruled this a pre-0.1.0 breaking change; gating a core binding representation would double every reflection/snapshot/differential expectation for a toggle with no rollout story.

patches.title: Capture-shape idiom recognition (observationally invisible)

files.description: Add a capture-matching pattern element and registry entries: (a) a `.direct` entry for the two-form body `[<literal>, first(source-bound)]` whose selected handler verifies the first form is a one-element list and pushes its element directly, falling through to the generic path on any shape mismatch; (b) per-BinaryOp combinator-context entries `[capture, <op>]` and `[capture, swap, <op>]` that unwrap the captured element as the constant operand, reusing the existing constant/constant_left kernel machinery. Update the comptime registry array length.

Implement the patch-1 stub: build capture shapes exactly as programs do (`3 literal`, `3 (+) partial`, `3 (swap -) partial`), run recognized and generic paths over generated inputs including error-producing ones (overflow, type), and assert value equality, representation parity (brackets), error kind/payload equality, and bit-identical floats.

changes: Extend the pattern vocabulary so a capture matches exactly a one-element non-word list followed by the word `first` resolving to the source-defined core `first` (binding = .source, matching the existing rest_pattern discipline); any other resolution of `first` in the application environment falls through to the generic path — recognition guards must preserve full late-binding semantics.

The direct-context handler must validate the literal form is a list of length 1 at selection or execution time and fall back generically otherwise — `.literal` alone matches any non-word form, so the length check cannot be skipped.

Combinator entries mirror constant_operation_pattern/constant_swap_operation_pattern semantics with the captured element as the constant; set constant_left correctly for both orders and route through the same kernels the existing constant entries use.
Run `zig build differential` and the 1/N-worker suites; recognition must be unobservable at HEAD (the shapes are producible today via literal and partial).

patches.spec:
module ONE_BINDER_MERGE_PATCH_2.

> Capture-shape recognition is acceleration only: a recognized
> application is indistinguishable from the generic frame-machine path.

Quotation.
Context.
direct => Context.
combinator => Context.
Outcome.
capture-shaped? q: Quotation => Bool.
recognized? q: Quotation, c: Context => Bool.
generic-eval q: Quotation, c: Context => Outcome.
fused-eval q: Quotation, c: Context => Outcome.
---
> Recognition only ever fires on capture shapes.
all q: Quotation, c: Context | recognized? q c -> capture-shaped? q.
> The fused path is bit-identical to the generic path — values,
> representation, and error kind/payload alike (Outcome covers success
> and failure, so the equality is total over both arms).
all q: Quotation, c: Context | recognized? q c -> fused-eval q c = generic-eval q c.
> An unrecognized application always takes the generic path.
all q: Quotation, c: Context | ~(recognized? q c) -> fused-eval q c = generic-eval q c.

patches.spec:
module ONE_BINDER_MERGE_PATCH_3.

> The equivalence law: `v 'name set` is observationally
> `v literal (-- value) 'name def`. After this patch no language path publishes a
> value-kind binding; the union arm still exists but is unproducible.

Value.
Name.
Quotation.
Effect.
const-effect => Effect.
BindingKind.
word-kind => BindingKind.
Binding.
kind b: Binding => BindingKind.
body-of b: Binding => Quotation.
effect-of b: Binding => Effect.
capture v: Value => Quotation.
apply-capture q: Quotation, v: Value, q = capture v => Value.
set-bind v: Value, n: Name => Binding.
ScopeKind.
top-scope => ScopeKind.
module-root => ScopeKind.
setp-legal? s: ScopeKind => Bool.
---
> Every set publication is a word binding carrying the literal capture
> and the synthesized constant effect — uniformly in every scope.
all v: Value, n: Name | kind (set-bind v n) = word-kind.
all v: Value, n: Name | body-of (set-bind v n) = capture v.
all v: Value, n: Name | effect-of (set-bind v n) = const-effect.
> Applying a capture yields exactly the captured value (0 inputs,
> 1 output — the const-effect contract holds by construction).
all v: Value | apply-capture (capture v) v = v.

precedents.whyApplicable: The same answer in a modern concatenative vocabulary: constants are words defined by an ordinary defining word. Confirms the ergonomics of keeping a named sugar (set) rather than requiring users to hand-roll captures.

module ONE_BINDER_MERGE.

> ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
> THE GUARANTEE
> ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
> One binding kind: bare reference always applies the stored body.
> `v 'name set` is observationally `v literal (-- value) 'name def` — a word
> binding with body ((v) first) and synthesized effect (-- value),
> uniformly at top level and in modules. Reflection is honest and
> total; capture-shape recognition is invisible acceleration; the
> value arm is unrepresentable.

Value.
Name.
Quotation.
Effect.

WordBody.
Builtin.
NativeCallable.

TopPublication = WordBody.
ModulePublication = WordBody + NativeCallable.

capture v: Value => Quotation.
apply-capture q: Quotation, v: Value, q = capture v => Value.
set-bind v: Value, n: Name => WordBody.

all v: Value, n: Name | body-of (set-bind v n) = capture v.
all v: Value, n: Name | effect-of (set-bind v n) = const-effect.

setp-legal? module-root.
all s: ScopeKind | setp-legal? s -> s = module-root.
> Recognition is unobservable — total over success and failure outcomes.
all q: Quotation, c: Context | fused-eval q c = generic-eval q c.
